items.required_idea: The GFTA-3 standard score and percentile pair appears inconsistent and needs checking against the correct score type, test form, and norm table.
acceptable_alternatives: Flag the mismatch and ask to verify the official report/manual without guessing a replacement percentile.
do_not_require: A precise percentile conversion from memory
A diagnosis based only on this score
source_checks: Applicable GFTA-3 manual and norm table

items.required_idea: If 80 is a CELF-5 standard score and 40 is its percentile rank, the pair conflicts with Pearson's guide, which maps SS 80 to PR 9 for the relevant index score conversion example.
acceptable_alternatives: Ask to verify the score type/index and official report before changing a value.
do_not_require: A precise diagnosis or treatment decision from a composite score alone

items.required_idea: The SSI-4 row's score label and pairing of score, percentile, and severity need to be verified against the actual SSI-4 scoring protocol and age-appropriate norm group. The case does not include enough scoring details to supply a replacement.
acceptable_alternatives: Call it a possible scoring/reporting inconsistency and request the protocol, age norm, and test manual.
do_not_require: A guessed replacement score or severity classification

items.required_idea: The 4/10, 6/10, and 8/10 trial-like results are attributed to GFTA-3 or SSI-4 without describing standard administration/scoring. A treatment probe should be described separately with target, context, cueing, denominator, and scoring rule.
acceptable_alternatives: Ask whether these are informal probes mislabeled as test scores and recommend reporting formal assessment results separately.
do_not_require: A claim that the tests can never be used to monitor a client
source_checks: ASHA Assessment Tools, Techniques, and Data Sources

items.required_idea: The brief includes both /k/ and /t/, while the annual statement mentions /k/ only; the criterion remains a placeholder. Baseline/context/cueing and an appropriate measure are not specified.
acceptable_alternatives: Write separate measurable targets or explain why only /k/ is being targeted; define criterion and a suitable probe based on assessment.
do_not_require: Assuming /k/ or /t/ is an appropriate target without speech sample and language/dialect context
source_checks: ASHA Speech Sound Disorders Practice Portal

items.required_idea: Eye contact and a universally 'normal' pace are not justified by the information provided. A fluency goal should follow individualized assessment of communication impact and child/family priorities; eye contact should not be imposed as a proxy for communication success.
acceptable_alternatives: Suggest a child-valued participation/communication goal or a specific strategy only if assessment supports it.
do_not_require: Claiming that all rate-focused goals are wrong
A specific fluency diagnosis from the case alone
source_checks: ASHA Stuttering, Cluttering, and Fluency Practice Portal

items.required_idea: The receptive-language goal is vague, contains [X] placeholders, and does not define targets, context, supports, or success criteria. The clinical file does not establish the planned words or measurement rule.
acceptable_alternatives: Request baseline information and a goal tied to the assessment profile and functional need.
do_not_require: Knowing hidden generation metadata unless it is explicitly part of the student case
source_checks: ASHA Spoken Language Disorders Practice Portal

items.required_idea: The case lacks language/dialect history, actual communication samples, test form/conditions, functional impact, and child/family perspective. Ethnicity alone does not establish language use or test-norm fit.
acceptable_alternatives: Name concrete history questions and a culturally/linguistically appropriate, multi-source assessment plan.
do_not_require: Declaring a test invalid based solely on Hispanic/Latino identity
source_checks: ASHA Speech Sound Disorders Practice Portal

items.required_idea: Generation metadata requested expressive language while the visible case emphasizes receptive language. This is a dataset/provenance check, not a student finding unless the metadata is deliberately revealed.
The trailing unmatched brace appears to be a text artifact. It can be cleaned up but is not a clinical reasoning error.
